novel_features.name: Local macro diary + goal
novel_features.description: Log foods by barcode and track running kcal/protein/fat/carbs against a daily goal — free, offline, scriptable.
novel_features.rationale: OFF has no diary; this lives entirely in a local SQLite diary_entry/goal join. It is MyFitnessPal's paywalled core loop, rebuilt on open data.
novel_features.example: openfoodfacts-pp-cli diary add 3017620422003 --servings 1.5 && openfoodfacts-pp-cli diary today --agent
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs to track or total a user's intake without an account, subscription, or network round-trip per query.

novel_features.name: Range diary report
novel_features.description: Per-day macro totals and averages across a date range from the local diary.
novel_features.rationale: Time-windowed aggregation over local diary rows — no single OFF API call produces it.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when summarizing a week of intake or feeding macro trends into a planner.

novel_features.name: Side-by-side compare
novel_features.description: Put two or more products side-by-side on per-100g nutriments, Nutri-Score, NOVA, Eco-Score, and sugar.
novel_features.rationale: Multi-product client-side table built from N barcode lookups; no OFF tool ships compare.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this on store-brand-vs-name-brand or any 'which is healthier' decision.

novel_features.name: Healthier-alternative swap
novel_features.description: Given a product, find better-scoring items in the same category, ranked by Nutri-Score/NOVA.
novel_features.rationale: Reads the product's category, runs a Nutri-Score-sorted category search, and ranks mechanically — no tool answers 'find a healthier alternative in this category'.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when a user wants a concrete substitute, not just a verdict on what they're holding.

novel_features.name: Recipe/meal nutrition aggregation
novel_features.description: Sum per-serving nutriments across multiple products into one recipe block plus a per-serving block.
novel_features.rationale: Mechanical aggregation over batch lookups into agent-shaped JSON; OFF returns single products only.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an LLM meal-planner needs totaled nutrition for a composed dish.

novel_features.name: Allergen-profile alert
novel_features.description: Store your allergens once, then check any product (and exit non-zero on) one whose allergens or traces match.
novel_features.rationale: Set-intersection of product allergens/traces against a stored local profile with a scriptable exit code — no consumer app offers an allergen gate you can pipe.
novel_features.example: openfoodfacts-pp-cli allergens set milk,gluten && openfoodfacts-pp-cli allergens check 3017620422003
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use as a guardrail in any flow that must refuse foods matching a fixed allergen list.

novel_features.name: Diet-budget search
novel_features.description: Search constrained to the macros left in today's goal after what you've logged.
novel_features.rationale: Reads (goal − logged diary macros) from SQLite and injects the remaining headroom as nutrient-range filters on the live search — a cross-entity join of local state into an API query.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to suggest foods that still fit a user's remaining daily budget.

novel_features.name: Offline nutriment ranking
novel_features.description: Rank synced products in a category by any nutriment, entirely from the local store.
novel_features.rationale: Pure local SQLite query over the synced product/nutriment store — runs offline and dodges the rate limit.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for repeated comparisons across a category without burning the 10-req/min search budget.

narrative.headline: Every Open Food Facts read endpoint, plus a local calorie/macro diary, product compare, and offline search no other Open Food Facts tool has — free, no account, pipeable to jq.
narrative.value_prop: A general-purpose Go CLI for the Open Food Facts database: barcode lookup, filtered search, Nutri-Score/NOVA/Eco-Score, additives and allergens, with a built-in mandatory User-Agent and an adaptive rate limiter so you don't get throttled or banned. On top of the API it adds what the consumer apps charge for: a local SQLite food diary (diary), healthier-alternative lookup (swap), product comparison (compare), and offline ranking/search that bypass the rate limit entirely.
narrative.auth_narrative: No API key, no account, no OAuth. Open Food Facts read endpoints are open data. The only requirement is a well-formed User-Agent, which the CLI sets automatically and lets you override with --user-agent or OPENFOODFACTS_USER_AGENT.

quickstart.comment: Scan-and-judge: kcal, Nutri-Score, NOVA, additives, allergens for one barcode.
Find products by category tag against the live API, agent-shaped JSON.
Two products side-by-side on scores and per-100g nutriments.
Log a food to the local diary.
Running kcal/macro totals vs your daily goal.

troubleshoots.fix: You hit the per-IP rate limit (15/min reads, 10/min search). The CLI backs off automatically; for bulk work run `sync` once then query with `--local` / `rank` / `sql` offline.

troubleshoots.symptom: Requests rejected or empty as a suspected bot
troubleshoots.fix: Set a contactable User-Agent: `export OPENFOODFACTS_USER_AGENT='myapp/1.0 (me@example.com)'`. Run `doctor` to confirm it's set.

troubleshoots.symptom: Product has no Nutri-Score or missing nutriments
troubleshoots.fix: Open Food Facts data is crowd-sourced; many products are partial. Nutri-Score needs a category. The CLI emits null fields rather than failing — check `product <code> --fields nutriments,categories`.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent or script needs nutrition facts for a packaged food without an API key, account, or paid tier — barcode lookups, name search with nutrient filters, Nutri-Score/NOVA/additive/allergen data, or a local calorie/macro diary. It is the right choice over a raw HTTP call because it ships rate-limit safety, a mandatory User-Agent, offline search, and aggregation primitives (compare, recipe, diary) the bare API lacks.

recipes.title: Aisle verdict with allergen gate
recipes.command: openfoodfacts-pp-cli allergens set milk,gluten && openfoodfacts-pp-cli allergens check 3017620422003
recipes.explanation: Store your allergens once, then `allergens check` flags a HIT and exits non-zero when the product matches — a scriptable buy/skip gate.

recipes.title: Daily macro loop
recipes.command: openfoodfacts-pp-cli diary goal --kcal 2000 --protein 150 && openfoodfacts-pp-cli diary add 3017620422003 --servings 2 && openfoodfacts-pp-cli diary today --agent
recipes.explanation: Set a goal, log foods by barcode, and read running totals vs the goal — MyFitnessPal's core loop, free and offline.

recipes.title: Healthier swap in a category
recipes.explanation: Find better-scoring products in the same category as a given barcode, ranked by Nutri-Score.

recipes.title: Narrow a deep payload with --select
recipes.explanation: Search responses carry tens of KB per page; dotted --select paths return only the fields an agent needs, keeping context small.

recipes.title: Offline ranking without burning rate limit
recipes.command: openfoodfacts-pp-cli sync --resources find && openfoodfacts-pp-cli rank --sort sugar --agent
recipes.explanation: Sync a category to SQLite once, then rank by any nutriment offline — no repeated API calls, no throttling.
